labels.label: ex:take_closed_unit_disc

hypotheses.paper: M\S endowed with a hyperbolic metric
hypotheses.note: DEC-81 metric reading: GX.IsHyperbolicMetric — a metric on the (Isom H, H)-surface giving its topology, a length metric (paths of variation arbitrarily close to the distance), locally the Poincare metric read in the charts; it is unique (GX.IsHyperbolicMetric.unique). The Riemannian tensor (curvature -1) is not formalized: no Riemannian surfaces at this pin. DEC-84: the (Isom H, H)-atlas is data (ChartedSpace PoincareDisc + HasGroupoid gxGroupoid HypIsom) compatible with the metric (IsHyperbolicMetric.local_isometry).

DEC-84: the atlas is given as data compatible with the metric: IsHyperbolicMetric.local_isometry (locally m = d_H read in the charts); the hyperbolic metric is then unique (GX.IsHyperbolicMetric.unique).

metric completeness of m (IsCuspedHyperbolicMetric.complete); proved equivalent to Thurston-Goldman completeness (GX.IsHyperbolicMetric.completeSpace_iff): <= quotient metric of H (GX.IsHypQuotient), => Hopf-Rinow (geodesic lifting by completeness + mathlib's IsLocalHomeomorph.continuous_lift).

DEC-84 (author ruling): 'finite volume' reads as a hyperbolic cusp at each s in S (CuspChart + IsHyperbolicCusp, field IsCuspedHyperbolicMetric.cusp); each cusp is proved to have finite area (GX.CuspChart.cusp_finite_area, area 1/c of the strip, GX.volume_cuspStrip). The thick-thin step (finite volume => cusps) and the global area measure are not built and, by DEC-84, not owed.
M Hausdorff, locally path-connected, first countable, connected; genus not used
S finite carried; 2g-2+s>0 not used (it is the existence condition)

findings: Under DEC-81 + DEC-84 the row is certified in full by GX.take_closed_unit_disc_metric: every assertion of l.1879-1886 is proved for M\S with a complete hyperbolic metric, cusps at the points of S, atlas compatible with the metric.

Kept from WP-40b: metric completeness is exactly Thurston-Goldman completeness (GX.IsHyperbolicMetric.completeSpace_iff), so 'complete' may be read either way; finite volume enters the paper's argument only through the cusp shape of the ends (thick-thin), which DEC-84 takes as the reading.

Carried over from WP-35i: l.1880 'injective developing map' holds for every developing map; l.1881 the neighbourhoods U ≅ {r<r0} exist arbitrarily small (not every open neighbourhood); l.1882 D(U) is a horodisc together with its centre D(x) on the circle.

kb_proposals: A ruling that accepts a reading already encoded in a strict structure closes the row by docstring re-marking only: no statement change, so downstream names stay stable.
